He had a significant amount of wealth and influence, as indicated by his correspondence with Shipti-Ishar. One of the most famous aspects of Ea-Nasir's story is his refusal to provide a loan to Shipti-Ishar, despite their long-standing business relationship. This refusal is documented in one of the letters and has been the subject of scholarly debate regarding the nature of their relationship and the reasons behind Ea-Nasir's decision.

The "Ur Letters" are an important source of information for historians and archaeologists studying the ancient Near East, and Ea-Nasir's role in these letters has contributed to our understanding of the economic and social structures of the time.
